title: Pipkin and the Sunshine Plant
markdown:
The warm afternoon sun dappled the garden. Toby and Auntie Flo were busy with the flowers. Pipkin the hamster sat on Toby’s shoulder, nose wiggling.

“Oh dear,” Flo pointed to a little plant. “This friend looks tired. Leaves aren’t bright green.”

Pipkin whispered, “Why is he sad?”

Flo knelt. “Plants need special things. This friend likes shade, but maybe he’s missing something.”

A soft sunbeam peeked through the apple tree and landed on a pale leaf. Pipkin felt its warmth. “It’s warm!”

Flo’s eyes twinkled. “Leaves are like tiny kitchens. Sunshine is a special ingredient. It helps them make their strength and stay green.” Pipkin watched the beam, feeling the gentle heat on his own fur.

Toby nodded. “So if he’s in too much shade, he can’t get his sunshine food?”

“Exactly. Gentle light — not too much, enough to feel his best.”

They moved the pot with care. Apple-tree shade, but soft sunbeams could reach the leaves a little while each day. Pipkin watched, heart full of hope, and counted the minutes of light on his claws as if that might help.

Slowly the pale leaves unfurled, stretching like after a long nap. A soft green glow returned. Whiskers twitched. “Look! He’s waking up!”

Flo whispered that the leaves were drinking sunshine, making food to grow strong — the tiny kitchen at work. She did not send Pipkin hunting other sunshine secrets or into peaceful dreams on the page.

Pipkin snuggled into Toby’s shoulder. The plant stood happier, greener. Evening painted the sky sleepy colours. Toby set a pebble to mark the pot’s new spot so nobody would tuck it back into the deep shade by mistake. Pipkin checked the pebble twice, because hamsters like to be sure.
